title: Comparing and Ordering Rational Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Comparing and Ordering Rational Numbers Worksheets (TEKS 6.2C, 6.2D, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.2C locate, compare, and order integers and rational numbers using a number line; 6.2D order a set of rational numbers arising from mathematical and real-world contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.2C and 6.2D: compare and order integers, fractions and decimals on a number line, absolute value and order, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Numbers increase to the right on a number line.
key_sub: −3 > −7 because −3 is closer to 0. Write fractions and decimals in the same form to order them.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • On a number line, numbers increase to the right. The number farther right is greater.
  • Every positive number is greater than every negative number.
  • For two negative numbers, the one closer to 0 is greater: −3 > −7.
  • To order fractions and decimals, write them in the same form, then place them on a number line.

Examples

Example

Order −2.5, 1/2, −3, 0 from least to greatest.

−3 is farthest left

then −2.5, then 0

1/2 is right of 0

Answer: −3, −2.5, 0, 1/2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking −7 > −3 because 7 > 3−7 is farther left, so −7 < −3.
Ordering by absolute value|−8| is large, but −8 is less than 2.
Comparing −1/2 and −0.4 without converting−1/2 = −0.5, which is less than −0.4.

items.q: Between which two integers is −3.4 on a number line?
items.e: −3.4 is a little more than 3 units to the left of 0. It is past −3 but not as far as −4: between −4 and −3.

items.q: What number is halfway between −5 and −4?

items.q: Where is −2 14 on a number line?
items.e: −2 14 is 14 past −2, going left. So it is between −3 and −2, closer to −2.

sets.title: Compare numbers on a number line

items.q: Which number is greater, −3 or −7? Why?
c: −3, because it is to the left of −7
−3, because it is to the right of −7
−7, because it is to the left of −3
items.e: −3 is to the right of −7 on the number line, so −3 > −7. Both are negative: the one farther from 0 (−7) is less. Being farther from 0 does not make a negative number greater.

items.q: Compare −1.5 and 0.5. Which statement is true?
items.e: −1.5 is to the left of 0.5 on the number line, so −1.5 < 0.5. A positive number is always greater than a negative number.

items.q: The statement −2 < 4 is true. What does it tell you about the number line?
c: −2 and 4 are the same distance from 0
items.e: “−2 < 4” means −2 is less than 4, so −2 is to the left of 4 on the number line.

items.q: Zoe ordered these numbers from least to greatest: −1, −4, −6, 2. Is she right?
items.e: Zoe put the negative numbers in order as if they were positive. −6 is farthest left, so it is the least: −6, −4, −1, 2.

items.q: Look at −4 and −9. Which statement is false?
items.e: −4 is to the right of −9, so −4 > −9, not −4 < −9. The other statements are true: |−4| = 4 and |−9| = 9, so |−4| < |−9|.

items.q:
Order the numbers from least to greatest absolute value.
−7,  3,  −1,  5
items.e: Find each absolute value: |−7| = 7, |3| = 3, |−1| = 1, |5| = 5. Closest to 0 comes first: −1, 3, 5, −7. This is not the same as ordering the numbers (−7, −1, 3, 5).

items.q: Which number is less than −5 but has an absolute value less than 9?
Compare 6 and −10. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: 6 is to the right of −10, so 6 > −10. Absolute value: |6| = 6 and |−10| = 10, so |6| < |−10|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q: Compare −1.5 and −0.5. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −1.5 is to the left of −0.5, so −1.5 < −0.5. Absolute value: |−1.5| = 1.5 and |−0.5| = 0.5, so |−1.5| > |−0.5|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q: Look at −12 and −5. Which statement is false?
items.e: −12 is to the left of −5, so −12 < −5, not −12 > −5. The other statements are true: |−12| = 12 and |−5| = 5, so |−12| > |−5|.

items.q: Which number is greater than −1 but has a greater absolute value than −1?
items.e: Check both parts for each number. 2: 2 > −1, |2| = 2; −2: −2 < −1, |−2| = 2; 0: 0 > −1, |0| = 0; −12: −12 > −1, |−12| = 12. Only 2 fits both.

items.q: Compare −12 and −5. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −12 is to the left of −5, so −12 < −5. Absolute value: |−12| = 12 and |−5| = 5, so |−12| > |−5|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q: Compare −3 and −8. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −3 is to the right of −8, so −3 > −8. Absolute value: |−3| = 3 and |−8| = 8, so |−3| < |−8|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q:
Order the numbers from least to greatest absolute value.
−12,  −3,  14,  2
c: −3, 2, −12, 14
14, −12, 2, −3
−3, −12, 14, 2
2, 14, −12, −3
items.e: Find each absolute value: |−12| = 12, |−3| = 3, |14| = 14, |2| = 2. Closest to 0 comes first: 14, −12, 2, −3. This is not the same as ordering the numbers (−3, −12, 14, 2).

items.q: Which number is greater than −6 but has a greater absolute value than −6?
items.e: Check both parts for each number. 8: 8 > −6, |8| = 8; −8: −8 < −6, |−8| = 8; 5: 5 > −6, |5| = 5; −5: −5 > −6, |−5| = 5. Only 8 fits both.

items.q: Compare −9 and 4. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −9 is to the left of 4, so −9 < 4. Absolute value: |−9| = 9 and |4| = 4, so |−9| > |4|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q:
Order the numbers from least to greatest absolute value.
2,  −6,  −4.5,  1
items.e: Find each absolute value: |2| = 2, |−6| = 6, |−4.5| = 4.5, |1| = 1. Closest to 0 comes first: 1, 2, −4.5, −6. This is not the same as ordering the numbers (−6, −4.5, 1, 2).

items.q: Which number is less than 3 but has a greater absolute value than 3?
items.e: Check both parts for each number. −4: −4 < 3, |−4| = 4; 4: 4 > 3, |4| = 4; 2: 2 < 3, |2| = 2; −2: −2 < 3, |−2| = 2. Only −4 fits both.

items.q: Compare −3 and 8. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −3 is to the left of 8, so −3 < 8. Absolute value: |−3| = 3 and |8| = 8, so |−3| < |8|.

items.q: Carlos says the number with the greater absolute value is always the greater number. Is he right?
c: Yes. It is true for every number.
items.e: It is not true for negative numbers. −8 is farther from 0 than 3, so |−8| > |3|. But −8 is to the left of 3, so −8 < 3.

items.q: Noah says |−9| < |4| because −9 < 4. Is he right?
c: Yes. −9 is to the left of 4.
items.e: −9 < 4 is about order. Absolute value is distance from 0: |−9| = 9 and |4| = 4, so |−9| > |4|.

items.q: Look at −7 and 2. Which statement is false?
items.e: −7 is to the left of 2, so −7 < 2, not −7 > 2. The other statements are true: |−7| = 7 and |2| = 2, so |−7| > |2|.

items.q: Elijah says −10 > −2 because 10 > 2. Is he right?
c: No. −10 is to the left of −2, so −10 < −2.
items.e: 10 > 2 compares the absolute values: |−10| > |−2|. For the numbers themselves, −10 is to the left of −2, so −10 < −2.

items.q: At 7 a.m., it was −4 °F in Fargo and 2 °F in Omaha. Which statement is true?
items.e: −4 is to the left of 2 on a thermometer number line, so −4 < 2. The lower temperature is colder: Fargo was colder.

items.q: The low temperatures for four days were: Monday −3 °C, Tuesday −8 °C, Wednesday 1 °C, Thursday −5 °C. Which day was the coldest?
items.e: The coldest day has the least temperature. From least to greatest: −8 °C, −5 °C, −3 °C, 1 °C. −8 °C is the least, so Tuesday was the coldest.

items.q: A freezer must stay colder than −5 °F. Which temperature is colder than −5 °F?
items.e: Colder means less. −7 < −5, because −7 is to the left of −5. So −7 °F is colder. (−3 > −5, so −3 °F is warmer.)

items.q: Lucia’s bank account balance is −$30. Marcus’s balance is −$20. Who owes more money?
c: Marcus, because −$20 is a debt of $20
Lucia, because −$30 is a debt of $30
items.e: A negative balance is a debt. |−30| = 30, so Lucia owes $30. |−20| = 20, so Marcus owes $20. Lucia owes more, even though −$30 < −$20.

items.q: Which account balance shows a debt of more than $25?
items.e: A balance of −$30 is a debt of $30, and 30 > 25. −$20 is a debt of $20, −$25 is a debt of exactly $25, and $30 is not a debt. A balance less than −$25 means a debt greater than $25.

items.q: Diego’s account balance is −$45. How much money does he owe?
items.e: A negative balance is a debt. The size of the debt is the absolute value: |−45| = 45. He owes $45.

items.q: Four friends have these account balances: $15, −$40, −$10, $0. Order the balances from least to greatest.
items.e: The biggest debt is the least balance. From least to greatest: −$40, −$10, $0, $15. −$40 < −$10 because a debt of $40 is more than a debt of $10.

items.q: A diver is at −40 feet. A submarine is at −120 feet. Which one is deeper?
c: They are at the same depth
items.e: Deeper means lower. −120 is to the left of (below) −40, so −120 < −40. The submarine is deeper: 120 feet below sea level.

items.q: A fish is swimming at an elevation of −18 feet. How far below sea level is it?
items.e: Sea level is 0. The distance from 0 is the absolute value: |−18| = 18. The fish is 18 feet below sea level.

items.q: A bird is flying at 25 feet. A fish is swimming at −30 feet. Which one is farther from sea level?
c: The bird, because it is above sea level
They are the same distance from sea level
items.e: Distance from sea level is absolute value. |−30| = 30 and |25| = 25. 30 > 25, so the fish is farther from sea level, even though 25 > −30.

items.q: Four places have these elevations: a beach at 0 feet; a valley at −86 feet; a hill at 120 feet; a mine tunnel at −250 feet. Which place is the lowest?
items.e: The lowest place has the least elevation. −250 < −86 < 0 < 120, so the mine tunnel is the lowest.

items.q: In golf, the lowest score wins. Ximena’s score is −3. Grace’s score is −1. Who wins?
items.e: −3 is to the left of −1, so −3 < −1. The lowest score wins, so Ximena wins.

items.q: In golf, a lower score is better. Four players scored −2, 1, −5, 0. Order the scores from best to worst.
items.e: Best to worst means least to greatest: −5, −2, 0, 1. −5 is the best score because it is the least.

items.q: At noon, the temperature was −6 °F. At midnight, it was −11 °F. Which statement is true?
c: −6 < −11, so it was colder at noon
−11 > −6, so it was colder at noon
−11 > −6, so it was colder at midnight
−11 < −6, so it was colder at midnight
items.e: −11 °F is farther below 0 than −6 °F, so −11 < −6. The lower temperature is colder: midnight.

items.q: One morning, it was −9 °F in Anchorage and −2 °F in Denver. Which city’s temperature was closer to 0 °F?
c: They were the same distance from 0 °F
items.e: Closer to 0 means the smaller absolute value. |−9| = 9 and |−2| = 2. 2 < 9, so Denver was closer to 0 °F.

items.q: In a football game, a team gained 5 yards on one play (+5) and lost 7 yards on the next play (−7). On which play did the ball move a greater distance?
c: Both plays moved the ball the same distance
The first play, because a gain is always more
items.e: Distance is absolute value: |5| = 5 and |−7| = 7. 7 > 5, so the ball moved farther on the second play, even though 5 > −7.

items.q: Gabriel has a balance of −$12, Ava has $3, Harper has −$40, and Josiah has $0. Who has the greatest balance?
items.e: The greatest balance is the one farthest right on a number line: −$40 < −$12 < $0 < $3. Ava has the greatest balance, $3. Harper has the greatest debt, not the most money.

items.q: Thermometer A shows −2.5 °C. Thermometer B shows −1.5 °C. Which thermometer shows the colder temperature?
items.e: −2.5 is to the left of −1.5, so −2.5 < −1.5. The lower temperature is colder: Thermometer A.

items.q: The low temperature on Monday was −7 °F. On Tuesday, the low was even colder. Which could be Tuesday’s low?
items.e: Colder means less than −7, so the number must be to the left of −7. −9 < −7, so −9 °F could be Tuesday’s low. −5 °F is warmer, because −5 > −7.

items.q: Sofia’s account balance is less than −$50. What does this tell you about her debt?
c: She does not owe any money
items.e: A balance less than −$50 is to the left of −$50, like −$60. That is farther from 0, so the debt is more than $50.
